choices.label: Take notes on all of it
choices.result: Every point goes in your notebook, and you ask about the ones that sting. You leave with a summer plan and the feeling that the coach is actually on your side.

choices.label: Ask for the three hardest truths
choices.result: {coach} gives you three without softening them: your plant foot drifts, you look rattled after misses, and you don't lift enough. You work on all three until August.

choices.label: Bring your own review
choices.result: Your own review is four handwritten pages, and half of it matches theirs. The coach is impressed you thought about it, and {holder} laughs that you graded yourself harder.

scenarios.title: The Offseason Without Structure
scenarios.text: For the first time in your life, nobody tells you what to do all summer. No coach, no schedule, no bell. The facility is closed for six weeks, and your phone is very quiet.

authoring.premise: For the first time in your life, nobody tells you what to do all summer.

choices.label: Write your own program
choices.result: Twelve weeks, written by hand and taped to the fridge, and you follow it to the day. It's lonely work, and you report to camp stronger than anyone expected.

choices.label: Disappear for three weeks
choices.result: Three weeks with no ball, no film and no phone. It feels wrong for five days and wonderful after, and you come back to the field genuinely hungry.

choices.label: Train with {best_friend}
choices.result: {best_friend} drives up for a month and holds for you every morning in a city park. It's real work and a lot of laughing, and neither of you wants it to end.

scenarios.title: The Old College Rival
scenarios.text: A kicker you competed against all through college has signed with a club in your division. You'll be on the same field twice a year, and the local paper has already noticed.

authoring.premise: A kicker you competed against in college is now on a rival club.

choices.label: Text him before the first game
choices.result: A text the week before your first game against his club. You have dinner afterward and laugh about the college stuff that once felt huge.

choices.label: Use the rivalry
choices.result: Fuel, all week: the old rivalry gives every practice a little extra. He doesn't know, and you don't tell him.

choices.label: Study his film
choices.result: His film, studied closely, and you learn something about your own hips from the way he sets up. You send him a thank-you he doesn't understand.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Hazing Report
scenarios.text: A reporter asks you, on the record, about the club's rookie traditions. There's a story going around the league about another club's hazing, and she wants to know about yours.

authoring.premise: A reporter asks you, on the record, about the rookie traditions.

choices.label: Keep it to pastries and pads
choices.result: Pastries and pads, mostly, you explain, smiling. It's true, it's enough, and the captains notice you didn't give her anything else.

choices.label: Name the one that should change
choices.result: The one tradition that made you uncomfortable should change, you say carefully, without names. The captains agree, quietly, and change it.

choices.label: Keep the locker room private
choices.result: The locker room stays private, you say politely. She writes that the rookies 'declined to comment', and the story moves on.

scenarios.title: The Fan Who Sends Gifts
scenarios.text: A fan sends gifts to the facility every week, addressed to you: candy, then socks, then a framed painting of you as a medieval knight. The notes are getting longer.

authoring.premise: A fan sends gifts to the facility every week, and they're getting stranger.

choices.label: Tell security
choices.result: The club's security staff hears about it from you. They handle it kindly and firmly, and the knight painting goes in a storage room.

choices.label: Send one thank-you
choices.result: One thank-you note, warm and clear, asking them to stop sending gifts. It works, and you keep the painting, secretly.

choices.label: Ignore the gifts
choices.result: Ignored. The gifts keep coming, then the letters do, and by December you're a little uneasy every time the mailroom calls.

scenarios.title: Your First Endorsement Shoot
scenarios.text: Your first commercial shoot takes eleven hours in a warehouse for fifteen seconds of you holding a sports drink and saying one line. The director keeps saying 'more joy'.

authoring.premise: The commercial shoot takes eleven hours for fifteen seconds.

choices.label: Nail every take
choices.result: Every take, nailed, with more joy each time. The director asks you back for the next campaign and calls you 'a natural', which is a lie.

choices.label: Make the crew laugh
choices.result: The crew, laughing between takes, is the best part of the day. The makeup artist gives you their number for the next shoot.

choices.label: Just survive it
choices.result: Survived, barely, eleven hours of 'more joy'. Your face hurts from smiling, you sleep in the car on the way home, and you never watch the ad.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Wants Your Spot
scenarios.text: An undrafted kicker in camp keeps showing up early and kicking where you can see: long ones, clean ones, every morning, with a little look over his shoulder.

authoring.premise: An undrafted kicker in camp keeps showing up early and kicking where you can see.

choices.label: Show up earlier
choices.result: Earlier. He shows up earlier still. By the end of camp you're both kicking in the dark, and you've both gotten better.

choices.label: Give him a tip
choices.result: A tip about his plant foot, freely given. He thanks you sincerely and still wants your job, which you respect.

choices.label: Stay with your charts
choices.result: Your charts, your routine, nothing else. The coaches notice how calm you are while he keeps glancing over his shoulder at you.

scenarios.title: The New Club as a Rookie
scenarios.text: Released after your first camp and signed somewhere new three days later, you walk into a building where nobody knows your name, your locker still has the last kicker's tape on it, and the season starts Sunday.

authoring.premise: Released after your first camp and signed somewhere new, you start your rookie year over.

choices.label: Learn the building by Friday
choices.result: Every name in the building is yours by Friday: trainers, equipment staff, the snapper's kids. Nobody owes you anything here, and by the first game that has started to change.

choices.label: Kick like it's still a tryout
choices.result: Every rep in practice is a tryout, because it still is. Your leg is tired by Thursday, and the coaches stop watching you like a stranger who might leave.

choices.label: Find out what they saw
choices.result: {coach} pulls up your college film and shows you the three kicks that got you signed. It's a short list, and you build your whole first month around it.

scenarios.title: The First Time You Hear Boos
scenarios.text: Fans boo at a practice that's open to the public, after you miss two in a row in front of the bleachers. There are maybe three hundred people, and you know exactly who they mean.

authoring.premise: Fans boo at a practice open to the public, and you know who they mean.

choices.label: Answer with the next ten
choices.result: The next ten kicks go through. The boos stop somewhere around number six, and by number ten somebody in the bleachers is clapping.

choices.label: Wave at the boo section
choices.result: A big, friendly wave at the boo section. They laugh, and so do you, and one of them asks for an autograph after practice.

choices.label: Ask for a tool for crowd noise
choices.result: The team psychologist gives you one tool for crowd noise: a word, a breath, a spot on the ball. It works the next week.

scenarios.title: The Phone Call Home
scenarios.text: You call home every Sunday at six, and this Sunday, after a bad week, you don't know what to say. {parent} answers on the first ring, like always.

authoring.premise: You call home every Sunday, and this Sunday you don't know what to say.

choices.label: Tell him the truth
choices.result: You're struggling, you tell him. {parent} says he's proud of you anyway, and the way he says it, you believe him for the first time in a month.

choices.label: Talk about anything else
choices.result: The weather, his garden, the neighbor's new fence: an hour of anything else but football. It helps more than you expected it to.

choices.label: Ask about his hardest year
choices.result: How did he get through his hardest year? He tells you, slowly, things you never knew, and you write it down after you hang up.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Paycheck Math
scenarios.text: Late one night you do the math on your rookie contract, on the back of an envelope: the average career, the taxes, the agent's cut. The number at the bottom is smaller than you thought.

authoring.premise: You do the math on your rookie contract and realize how short a career really is.

choices.label: Make a five-year plan
choices.result: A five-year plan, made with your agent and an honest financial advisor. It's dull and comforting, like a good warmup.

choices.label: Make every season count
choices.result: Every season has to count, you decide, and you add an extra workout every week. The envelope goes on your fridge.

choices.label: Put the envelope away
choices.result: The envelope goes in a drawer, and you try not to think about it. You sleep less well than you'd like.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Calls Home Crying
scenarios.text: A rookie in your class calls home after every practice, in the parking lot, sometimes in tears. The veterans have started to notice, and one of them has started doing an impression.

authoring.premise: A rookie in your class calls home after every practice, and the veterans have noticed.

choices.label: Sit with him at lunch
choices.result: Lunch together, every day. He calls home a little less and laughs a little more, and by November he's doing impressions of the veteran.

choices.label: Ask the veterans to ease up
choices.result: The veterans, asked quietly to ease up. One of them tells you about his own first year, when he called home every night too.

choices.label: Let him find his way
choices.result: He'll find his way, you decide, and you mind your own business. He makes it through, barely, and never quite trusts the room.

scenarios.title: The Fourth Season
scenarios.text: Your fourth pro season. Nobody calls you a rookie anymore, the equipment manager knows your cleat size by heart, and two of this year's rookies ask for your autograph.

authoring.premise: Your fourth pro season, and nobody calls you a rookie anymore.

choices.label: Look out for the rookies
choices.result: The rookies get looked after, the way someone once looked after you: rides, meals, the names of the people who matter.

choices.label: Raise your own bar
choices.result: Nobody else will raise your bar now, so you do it yourself: new goals, written down and taped to the bathroom mirror.

choices.label: Enjoy the ease
choices.result: Some ease, finally earned. You enjoy this season more than any before it, and the snapper says you look five years younger.

scenarios.title: The Comfortable Routine
scenarios.text: Your routine works so well it's starting to feel like a rut. Same breakfast, same warmup, same thoughts at the same moments. You haven't felt nervous in a month, and you miss it.

authoring.premise: Your routine works so well it's starting to feel like a rut.

choices.label: Change one small thing
choices.result: One small change: a different song in your warmup. It's enough to wake you up, and your first kick that day feels new.

choices.label: Push harder inside it
choices.result: Harder, inside the exact same routine. It's tiring, and it works, and slowly the rut starts to feel like a groove again.

choices.label: Trust the rut
choices.result: A rut that works is a groove, you decide, and you trust it. The season goes on quietly and well.

scenarios.title: The Raise
scenarios.text: Your second contract is real money, and everyone you know has noticed: old friends with ideas, cousins with emergencies, a teacher from middle school with a fundraiser.

authoring.premise: Your second contract is real money, and everyone you know has noticed.

choices.label: Set one rule for everyone
choices.result: One rule, for everyone, written down. It's fair, it's a little lonely, and the calls slow down within a month.

choices.label: Help the ones who need it
choices.result: The people who really need it get help, quietly, and nobody else hears about it. {parent} finds out anyway and is proud.

choices.label: Change your number
choices.result: A new phone number, given to twelve people. Things get quieter immediately, and two old friends feel shut out and say so.

scenarios.title: The House With a Yard
scenarios.text: You buy a house with a backyard big enough for a kicking net. The previous owners left a swing set, a lemon tree and a note wishing you luck.

authoring.premise: You buy a house with a yard big enough for a kicking net.

choices.label: Put up the net
choices.result: The net goes up the first weekend. The neighbors watch from their windows, and by Sunday their kids are shagging balls for you.

choices.label: Throw a housewarming
choices.result: Everyone, over, the first Saturday: family, teammates, neighbors. {parent} gives the tour twice, and {sibling} falls off the swing set.

choices.label: Sit under the lemon tree
choices.result: Nothing, in the backyard, under the lemon tree, for a whole afternoon. It's the first time in years you've done nothing on purpose.

scenarios.title: The Specialist Who Retires
scenarios.text: The punter you've worked beside for six years retires suddenly, with a two-line statement on a Tuesday afternoon. He hasn't returned anyone's calls since, including yours.

authoring.premise: The punter you've worked beside for years retires suddenly.

choices.label: Throw him a send-off
choices.result: A send-off with the specialists at his favorite diner, whether he likes it or not. He comes, finally, and it's loud and long.

choices.label: Help the new punter settle
choices.result: The new punter gets your time and the old punter's tricks, passed along. The unit stays steady through the change.

choices.label: Give him his quiet
choices.result: His quiet, respected. You send one short message and wait, and a month later he calls you first, from a lake.

scenarios.title: A Different Snap
scenarios.text: A new long snapper arrives, and for the first time in years your timing is off. The ball comes faster, flatter, with a spin you don't recognize, and the misses are in practice for everyone to see.

authoring.premise: A new long snapper, and your timing is off for the first time in years.

choices.label: Rep it out after practice
choices.result: After every practice, an extra fifty snaps until the timing is back. Your leg is heavy and your rhythm returns by week three.

choices.label: Get to know him first
choices.result: Off the field first: dinners, his family, his terrible music. The timing follows the trust, the way it always does, within two weeks.

choices.label: Film every snap
choices.result: Every snap, filmed and studied. You find the tenth of a second in the film room, and fix it in one afternoon.

scenarios.title: The Pregnancy
scenarios.text: {love_interest} is pregnant, and the due date falls right in the middle of the season. You're thrilled, terrified, and already counting weeks on the team schedule.

authoring.premise: {love_interest} is pregnant, and the due date is in the middle of the season.

choices.label: Plan to be there
choices.result: You tell {coach} now that you'll miss a game if the baby comes on a Sunday. The coach says it's the right call and means it.

choices.label: Make a plan with everyone
choices.result: You make a plan with {love_interest}, the coach and both families: who's on call, which flights, which bags. It feels like a playbook, and it helps.

choices.label: Hope for the bye week
choices.result: You hope the baby comes in the bye week. You also keep a bag packed in the car and check your phone at every break.

scenarios.title: The Baby's First Year
scenarios.text: Sleepless nights with a newborn, in the middle of the season. The baby wakes at two and four, practice starts at eight, and you've started falling asleep in film sessions.

authoring.premise: Sleepless nights with a newborn during the season.

choices.label: Take the night shifts
choices.result: The night shifts on your off days, every one. You're tired and closer to {love_interest} and the baby than you've ever been to anyone.

choices.label: Sleep in shifts by schedule
choices.result: A sleep schedule, written on the fridge like a practice plan. It works, roughly, and nobody falls asleep in a meeting again.

choices.label: Ask the grandparents for help
choices.result: The grandparents, invited for a month. Everyone sleeps, the house is loud and full, and {parent} becomes a diaper expert.

scenarios.title: The Daycare
scenarios.text: Finding daycare in a city where you might not live next year. Every good place has a waiting list, and every waiting list asks how long you'll be in town.

authoring.premise: Finding daycare in a city where you might not live next year.

choices.label: Visit every place
choices.result: Six daycares, visited in one week, with a notebook. You pick the best one and get on the list by being honest about the contract.

choices.label: Ask the team families
choices.result: The other team families, asked at the next game. They have a list, a group chat and a spot opening up in March.

choices.label: Hire a nanny for the season
choices.result: A nanny for the season, and a decision later. It's expensive and easy, and the baby adores her within a week.

scenarios.title: The In-Laws
scenarios.text: {love_interest}'s family visits for two weeks during the season: parents, a grandmother, and a brother-in-law who is certain that kicking is easy and has a lot of advice about it.

authoring.premise: {love_interest}'s family visits for two weeks during the season.

choices.label: Be the perfect host
choices.result: Every evening at home with them: dinners, card games, the grandmother's long stories. {love_interest} notices, and so does the grandmother.

choices.label: Keep your routine
choices.result: Your routine, unchanged, and you see them at dinner every night. It's polite and a little distant, and {love_interest} doesn't say anything.

choices.label: Plan their days
choices.result: Their days, planned by you: the museum, the stadium tour, a lake. Everyone has something to do, and the brother-in-law gets a practice pass.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Video Series
scenarios.text: You start a video series teaching kids how to kick, filmed in your backyard on a phone. The first episode has more views than your team's highlight reel.

authoring.premise: You start a video series teaching kids how to kick.

choices.label: Make it really good
choices.result: Real drills, real mistakes, real fixes, and a lot of editing late at night. Coaches start using it in practice.

choices.label: Bring {holder} in
choices.result: {holder}, invited for an episode on holding. It's the most popular one by far, because {holder} is much funnier on camera than you.

choices.label: Keep it simple
choices.result: One video a month on your phone, unedited. It's honest and charming, and it never takes more than an hour.

scenarios.title: The Podcast Guest Spot
scenarios.text: A popular podcast wants you as a weekly guest. The host likes controversy and has a reputation for getting athletes to say things about their teammates.

authoring.premise: A podcast wants you every week, and the host likes controversy.

choices.label: Set your terms first
choices.result: Terms, agreed up front: no teammates, no coaches, no locker room. It's good radio anyway, and the host respects the line.

choices.label: Say yes and wing it
choices.result: Yes, and you're great at it, until the fourth episode, when you say too much about a teammate. You apologize to him in person.

choices.label: Pass on the podcast
choices.result: No podcast this year. The host finds another kicker, who says something he regrets by October, and you're quietly relieved.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Becomes a Friend
scenarios.text: A teammate has become your closest friend in the league: same humor, same bad taste in movies, families who get along. You realize it on a road trip, laughing at three in the morning.

authoring.premise: A teammate becomes your closest friend in the league.

choices.label: Make time for it
choices.result: Time, made on purpose: dinners, families, the off days together. The friendship becomes the best part of the whole job.

choices.label: Train together all summer
choices.result: A whole summer of training together, every morning. You both get better, and the friendship gets a rhythm of its own.

choices.label: Keep it easy
choices.result: No effort required, and none spent. Some friendships don't need any work at all, and this one never does, even years later.

scenarios.title: The Holder's Wedding
scenarios.text: {holder} asks you to be in the wedding party. It's in June, in {holder}'s hometown, and there's a rehearsal dinner where you're expected to say something.

authoring.premise: {holder} asks you to be in the wedding party.

choices.label: Say yes and give a toast
choices.result: Yes, and a toast at the rehearsal dinner that nobody forgets: the first hold, the bad haircut, the night they saved your season.

choices.label: Organize the weekend
choices.result: The whole weekend, organized by you: the hotel block, the shuttle, the backup suits. {holder} doesn't lift a finger and cries about it.

choices.label: Show up and enjoy it
choices.result: Showing up, standing where they tell you, dancing badly at the reception. You enjoy every minute, and {holder} says it was perfect.

scenarios.title: The Fan Club
scenarios.text: Fans start an official fan club in your name, with T-shirts and a newsletter. They want you at the first meeting, in the back room of a pizza place on a Tuesday.

authoring.premise: Fans start an official fan club, and they want you at the first meeting.

choices.label: Go to the meeting
choices.result: Two hours in the back room of the pizza place. They make you an honorary member, and the T-shirt becomes your favorite shirt.

choices.label: Send a message and a ball
choices.result: A recorded message and a signed ball for the raffle. They play the message three times and frame the ball.

choices.label: Thank them online
choices.result: A thank-you post, and your Tuesday stays your own. The club grows anyway, without you, which feels a little strange and kind of nice.

scenarios.title: The Rival's Big Contract
scenarios.text: {tyler} signs a bigger contract than yours, by a lot, and the media want a comment. A reporter reads you the number, slowly, and waits.

authoring.premise: {tyler} signs a bigger contract than yours, and the media want a comment.

choices.label: Congratulate him
choices.result: Congratulations, publicly, and you mean it. He texts you thanks within the hour and a photo of the two of you at seventeen.

choices.label: Decline to comment
choices.result: No comment, politely, and you walk away from the cameras. It makes a headline anyway: 'Kicker silent on rival's huge new deal.'

choices.label: Keep the number private
choices.result: The number, written on a card, goes inside your locker where only you can see it. Every practice that month has a little more in it.

scenarios.title: The Charity Golf Tournament
scenarios.text: You host your own charity golf tournament for the first time: thirty-six foursomes, a silent auction, and a sponsor who keeps asking for 'more visibility'.

authoring.premise: You host a charity golf tournament for the first time.

choices.label: Run it yourself
choices.result: Every detail, run by you, from the sign-up sheet to the last trophy. You're exhausted, and the tournament raises twice the goal.

choices.label: Invite the old college crew
choices.result: Your college teammates, invited, and {best_friend} runs the auction. It turns into a reunion, and the bidding gets very competitive.

choices.label: Find a sponsor to run it
choices.result: A sponsor who covers everything and handles the details. It raises more than you'd have alone, and feels less like yours.

scenarios.title: The Investment Club
scenarios.text: A group of teammates forms an investment club: monthly meetings, a shared account, a lot of opinions about technology stocks. They want you in, and the first meeting is at the quarterback's house.

authoring.premise: A group of teammates forms an investment club and wants you in.

choices.label: Join the club
choices.result: Joined. The meetings are mostly jokes and some good ideas, and the account does fine, and the friendships do better.

choices.label: Join with limits
choices.result: In, with a small amount and one rule: nothing you don't understand. You end up explaining index funds to a linebacker, who becomes your biggest convert.

choices.label: Keep money and friends apart
choices.result: Money and friends don't mix, for you. You stay out, politely, and still go to the meetings for the food.

scenarios.title: The Second Car
scenarios.text: You buy a second car on a whim after a good week, a convertible in a color the salesman called 'victory'. Then you realize you haven't driven the first one in a month.

authoring.premise: You buy a second car, and then realize you never drive the first one.

choices.label: Sell one of them
choices.result: One of them goes back on the market by Friday, at a loss. You feel smarter for it, and a little silly every time you see a convertible.

choices.label: Give the old one to {sibling}
choices.result: The old car, keys and all, goes to {sibling}, who cries in the driveway and then honks the horn for ten straight seconds.

choices.label: Keep both cars
choices.result: Both stay. They sit side by side in the driveway, shining, and the insurance bill makes you laugh out loud in a bad way.

scenarios.title: The Contract Rumors
scenarios.text: Rumors say the club might not re-sign you next spring. A radio host says it, then a blog, then the guy who makes your sandwich at the deli near the facility.

authoring.premise: Rumors say the club might not re-sign you next spring.

choices.label: Answer with your leg
choices.result: No interviews, no reading, just kicking every day. The rumors get quieter by November, and the deli guy apologizes with a free sandwich.

choices.label: Ask the club directly
choices.result: A direct question to the general manager, in his office. The answer is honest and incomplete: they love you, and they're keeping options open.

choices.label: Talk it over at home
choices.result: A long evening at home, talking it through, agreeing not to look at houses in other cities yet. It helps more than any answer would.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Elections
scenarios.text: The players' union asks you to run for team representative. The last rep was traded the week after a tense meeting with management, and everybody remembers.

authoring.premise: The players' union asks you to run for team representative.

choices.label: Run for the job
choices.result: Elected, by a lot. Now the young players call you about everything, from pensions to parking, and management knows your name in a new way.

choices.label: Nominate someone better
choices.result: A teammate better suited to the job gets your nomination and your vote. He wins, does it well, and thanks you at the end-of-season dinner.

choices.label: Stay off the ballot
choices.result: Off the ballot. You have enough meetings already, and you'd rather spend the time on the field and with family.

scenarios.title: The Mid-Career Injury
scenarios.text: A torn muscle in practice, on a routine kick, with a sound you've only heard other people make. It's the first serious injury of your career, right in your prime.

authoring.premise: The first serious injury of your career, in your prime.

choices.label: Follow the rehab exactly
choices.result: Every step of the rehab, exactly as written, for ten weeks. It's slow and dull, and you come back whole, which the trainers call rare.

choices.label: Push the timeline
choices.result: Early, by three weeks. You're back on the field and not quite right, and you kick carefully all season, favoring the leg.

choices.label: Lean on the people at home
choices.result: The worst weeks, spent leaning on home: {parent} on the phone every night, {sibling} visiting with bad movies. It gets you through.

scenarios.title: The Rehab Partner
scenarios.text: You're rehabbing beside a teammate with the same injury, on the same table, at the same hours, with the same trainer. Whoever's back first will notice, and so will the coaches.

authoring.premise: You rehab alongside a teammate with the same injury.

choices.label: Make it a team
choices.result: You push each other every day and swap the bad days. You both come back, and you've got a friend for life.

choices.label: Race him back
choices.result: You race him back and win by a week. He shakes your hand, and something between you cools a little.

choices.label: Compare notes
choices.result: Notes compared every afternoon: what hurts, what helps, what the trainers said. You both come back smarter, and a little closer.

scenarios.title: The Long Offseason
scenarios.text: The longest offseason of your career: fourteen weeks with no games, no meetings and nowhere to be. By week two you've reorganized the garage twice.

authoring.premise: The longest offseason of your career, and you don't know what to do with it.

choices.label: Rest for real
choices.result: Real rest, for once: no plans, long walks and long naps. Your body thanks you, and the garage stays organized.

choices.label: Take a course
choices.result: A course in something you've always wondered about: woodworking, it turns out. You make a crooked table and love it.

choices.label: Travel with family
choices.result: Three weeks of travel with the people you love most. It's the longest you've been away from a ball since high school.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Kids' Camp
scenarios.text: You run a free camp for kids in your hometown: two days, two hundred kids, one field, a donated pallet of footballs and the old high school band.

authoring.premise: You run a free camp for kids in your hometown.

choices.label: Run every station
choices.result: Every station, run by you. You lose your voice by noon on day one and keep going in a whisper, and the kids love the whisper.

choices.label: Bring three teammates
choices.result: Three teammates, including {holder}. The kids lose their minds, and {holder} runs a holding clinic that's the hit of the weekend.

choices.label: Make it a yearly camp
choices.result: The high school becomes a partner, so the camp happens every year whether you're there or not. It's the most lasting thing you've built.

scenarios.title: The Mortgage
scenarios.text: Your first mortgage, and the papers are thicker than your playbook: forty pages of terms, a stack of signature tabs, and a loan officer who keeps calling you 'the athlete'.

authoring.premise: Your first mortgage, and the papers are thicker than your playbook.

choices.label: Read every page
choices.result: Every page, read, with questions about the three that matter. The loan officer is surprised and fixes one clause in your favor.

choices.label: Bring {parent} to the signing
choices.result: {parent} at the signing, with reading glasses and opinions. He's done this before and asks the questions you didn't know to ask.

choices.label: Sign where they point
choices.result: Signed where they point, every tab, in twenty minutes. You hope for the best, and for a year you're never quite sure what you agreed to.

scenarios.title: The Family Health Scare
scenarios.text: A family member gets scary news from a doctor while you're on a road trip two thousand miles away. {parent} calls at midnight, trying very hard to sound calm.

authoring.premise: A family member gets scary news while you're on a road trip.

choices.label: Fly home overnight
choices.result: A red-eye home, a day at the hospital, a red-eye back for the game. You're exhausted and glad, and the news turns out better than feared.

choices.label: Stay on the phone all night
choices.result: All night, on the phone with {parent} and the doctors, asking every question. By morning there's a plan, and you're part of it.

choices.label: Stay with the team and call
choices.result: With the team, calling every hour between meetings. It's the hardest week of your season, and {parent} says it helped to hear your voice.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Divorce
scenarios.text: A teammate's divorce is playing out in the locker room: phone calls in the hallway, a lawyer at the facility, and jokes from people who should know better.

authoring.premise: A teammate's divorce plays out in the locker room.

choices.label: Be there quietly
choices.result: Quietly there for him: rides, lunches, no questions. He says later you were the only one who never made it a thing.

choices.label: Keep the room kind
choices.result: The jokes stop when you're around, because you calmly make them stop. The room follows your lead, and he notices who did it.

choices.label: Keep out of his business
choices.result: His business, not yours. You keep out of it entirely, and he's fine with that, and you wonder sometimes if he needed more.

scenarios.title: The Charity Auction
scenarios.text: You donate an experience to a charity auction, a day at practice with you, and it sells for a fortune to a retired schoolteacher who has been saving for it for a year.

authoring.premise: You donate an experience to a charity auction, and the winner is very excited.

choices.label: Make it a full day
choices.result: A whole day: practice, lunch with the specialists, kicks on the stadium field. She cries twice, and so does {holder}.

choices.label: Do exactly what was promised
choices.result: Exactly what was promised, done well and warmly. She's thrilled, and writes the club a thank-you letter they print in the program.

choices.label: Bring the whole unit
choices.result: The whole specialist unit, recruited by you. She gets four for the price of one, and the punter teaches her to hold.

scenarios.title: The Brand Ambassador
scenarios.text: A sporting-goods brand wants you as its regional ambassador for three years: commercials, store openings, a signature cleat. The contract arrives with a pen taped to it.

authoring.premise: A brand wants you as its regional ambassador for three years.

choices.label: Sign for three years
choices.result: Three years, signed. It's steady money and a lot of store openings, and your signature cleat is ugly in a way you grow to love.

choices.label: Sign for one year
choices.result: One year, with an option for more. They agree, a little surprised, and you keep your freedom for the next negotiation and the one after.

choices.label: Pass on the cleat
choices.result: No contract. Three years is a long time, and the cleat really is ugly. A rival kicker signs instead, and you see his face at the mall.

scenarios.title: The Kicker Clinic Tour
scenarios.text: A kicking company wants you on a weekend clinic tour: eight cities, eight Saturdays, a thousand young kickers who all want to know what your secret is.

authoring.premise: A kicking company wants you on a weekend clinic tour.

choices.label: Do the whole tour
choices.result: All eight cities. You see a thousand young kickers and remember being one, and you lose your voice in the sixth city.

choices.label: Do the dates near home
choices.result: The three dates near home, and your own training the rest of the time. It's a good balance, and the kids in your hometown are thrilled.

choices.label: Keep your weekends
choices.result: No tour. Your weekends stay yours, and you spend them doing nothing much with the people you love most, which is the point.

scenarios.title: A New Boss on the Sideline
scenarios.text: A new head coach arrives and doesn't seem to think kickers matter. In his first team meeting he forgets the special teams entirely, and the punter writes it down.

authoring.premise: A new head coach arrives and doesn't seem to think kickers matter.

choices.label: Make him notice
choices.result: One practice at a time, you make him notice: the extra kicks, the clean operation, the timing. By October he knows your name and uses it.

choices.label: Ask for ten minutes
choices.result: Ten minutes in his office to explain what you actually do. He listens, genuinely surprised, and asks a good question at the end.

choices.label: Win the assistants first
choices.result: The assistants first, then the head coach follows. It takes a month, and it's the quieter way, and it works.

scenarios.title: The Team Leader Talk
scenarios.text: {coach} catches you after a meeting and asks you to speak up more in team meetings. 'They listen to you,' the coach says. 'You just don't say anything.'

authoring.premise: {coach} asks you to speak up more in team meetings.

choices.label: Speak at the next meeting
choices.result: At the next meeting, you speak: short, clear, about the special teams' mistakes and how to fix them. The room listens, and two veterans nod.

choices.label: Speak when it counts
choices.result: Only when you have something only a kicker can see, you agree. It happens twice that season, and both times it matters.

choices.label: Lead one on one instead
choices.result: Your way: one teammate at a time, after practice, in the parking lot. It's quieter and it works, and {coach} lets it go.

scenarios.title: The Team Trip Abroad
scenarios.text: The club plays a game overseas, and the trip is a week long: a different city, a different language, a different time zone, and a stadium that smells like rain.

authoring.premise: The club plays a game overseas, and the trip is a week long.

choices.label: See the city with the unit
choices.result: The city, explored with the specialists: museums, a market, a terrible bus tour. It's the best road trip of your career.

choices.label: Keep your routine exactly
choices.result: Your routine, kept to the minute, even at four in the morning local time. It's lonely and very steady, and your leg feels like home.

choices.label: Shift your sleep a week early
choices.result: A week early, at home, you start shifting your sleep an hour a night. You land ready while half the roster stumbles off the plane.

scenarios.title: The Jet Lag Game
scenarios.text: You're kicking in a different time zone, three hours off, and your body hasn't noticed. Your leg feels like it belongs to someone who's still asleep at home.

authoring.premise: You're kicking in a different time zone, and your body hasn't noticed yet.

choices.label: Follow the sleep plan
choices.result: The trainers' sleep plan, exactly: light, dark, water, no phone. By game day you feel almost normal, which is enough.

choices.label: Kick your legs awake
choices.result: Extra kicks the first morning, until your leg finally wakes up. It works, mostly, and you're tired by Saturday night.

choices.label: Sleep whenever you can
choices.result: Naps, whenever and wherever: the bus, the hotel lobby, a training table. You stop worrying about the clock, and the clock stops mattering.

scenarios.title: The Contract Bonus
scenarios.text: You hit a contract bonus on the last day of the season. Your agent calls to congratulate you and asks you, very seriously, to celebrate quietly.

authoring.premise: You hit a contract bonus, and your agent wants you to celebrate quietly.

choices.label: Put it all in savings
choices.result: The whole bonus, straight into savings, and you tell almost nobody about it. Your advisor sends a single word by text: 'Proud.'

choices.label: Treat the specialists
choices.result: A nice dinner for the specialists, on you, and nobody posts about it. {holder} gives a toast to 'the bonus we all earned'.

choices.label: Celebrate at home
choices.result: Takeout, a movie and a very long sleep at home. It's the quietest celebration in league history, and it's exactly right.

scenarios.title: The Wedding Planning
scenarios.text: Wedding planning in the middle of the season, and every decision is a phone call: flowers between meetings, the menu on the team bus, seating charts at midnight.

authoring.premise: Wedding planning during the season, and every decision is a phone call.

choices.label: Take every call
choices.result: Every call, even in the minutes between meetings. {love_interest} feels it, and the seating chart is perfect, and you're exhausted.

choices.label: Hire a planner
choices.result: A planner, hired, and the big decisions saved for Mondays. It works beautifully, and it costs more than the cake and the flowers combined.

choices.label: Leave it to {love_interest}
choices.result: Most of it, left to {love_interest} until the offseason. They manage it all, and they remember exactly who didn't help.

scenarios.title: The House Party You Host
scenarios.text: You host a team party at your new house, and by ten o'clock it's twice as big as planned. There are people in your backyard you've never met.

authoring.premise: You host a team party at your new house, and it gets bigger than planned.

choices.label: Set the rules early
choices.result: You set the rules at the door: rides home, nothing stupid, done by midnight. Everyone respects them, and the night stays fun.

choices.label: Enjoy it
choices.result: Running with it, you enjoy the whole night. Half the team is in your backyard, laughing, and you've never felt more like one of them.

choices.label: Shut it down early
choices.result: You shut it down early when it gets too big. A few teammates grumble on the way out, and nobody calls the police.

scenarios.title: Your Old Coach Visits
scenarios.text: Your college special teams coach visits practice and watches every kick from the sideline, arms crossed, the way he did when you were nineteen and terrified of him.

authoring.premise: Your college special teams coach visits practice and watches every kick.

choices.label: Spend the day with him
choices.result: The whole day with him: practice, lunch, the drive to the airport. He tells stories about you that you'd forgotten, some of them true.

choices.label: Ask for his notes
choices.result: His notes, please. He has one page, and one line on it is gold: your left arm drops on long kicks. You fix it in a week.

choices.label: Give him your best practice
choices.result: The best practice of your year, for an audience of one. He nods once at the end, which is the most he ever gave you.

scenarios.title: The Ball Boy
scenarios.text: A ball boy who's been at the facility as long as you have, since he was twelve, is going to college in the fall. He's the first in his family to go.

authoring.premise: A ball boy who's been here as long as you have is going to college.

choices.label: Throw him a send-off
choices.result: A send-off in the equipment room, organized by the specialists, with a cake shaped like a football and a card everybody signed.

choices.label: Write him a letter
choices.result: A recommendation letter, written carefully over a weekend. He gets the scholarship, and sends you a photo from his dorm.

choices.label: Shake his hand
choices.result: A handshake on his last day and a wish of good luck. He'll remember it, and you'll wish you'd done a little more.

scenarios.title: The Scrapbook
scenarios.text: {parent} keeps a scrapbook of every article ever written about you, back to the peewee league newsletter. He shows it to you on a visit, a little embarrassed, very proud.

authoring.premise: {parent} keeps a scrapbook of every article about you, and shows you.

choices.label: Go through every page
choices.result: Every page, together, at the kitchen table, all evening. He tells you what he was doing the day of every article, and you listen.

choices.label: Help him digitize it
choices.result: A weekend of scanning, so nothing gets lost in a flood or a fire. He insists on keeping the paper one too, and you agree.

choices.label: Laugh at the old haircuts
choices.result: A few favorites, and a lot of laughing at your old haircuts. It's a warm half hour, and he puts the book back on its shelf carefully.

scenarios.title: The Fan Who Grew Up
scenarios.text: A kid who held a cardboard sign with your name at your first pro practice is now in high school, a kicker, and pretty good. His coach emails to tell you.

authoring.premise: A kid who held a sign at your first practice is now in high school and kicking.

choices.label: Invite him to practice
choices.result: An invitation to watch practice, and a session with you after. He kicks better than you did at sixteen, and you tell him so.

choices.label: Send a message about the sign
choices.result: A message: the sign is still on your fridge. He posts it, and his whole school sees it by lunch.

choices.label: Watch his videos
choices.result: His game film, watched from your couch, with a smile. You don't reach out, and you check his scores every Friday.

scenarios.title: The Fitness Test
scenarios.text: The club's offseason fitness test: shuttle runs, a mile, a jump. You're not where you were, the strength coach writes your times down without comment, and the linemen are watching.

authoring.premise: The club's offseason fitness test, and you're not where you were.

choices.label: Train for the retest
choices.result: Three weeks of training for the retest, and you pass it clean, faster than last year. The linemen cheer, sarcastically and then sincerely.

choices.label: Explain kicking fitness
choices.result: Your leg numbers, shown to the trainers: kicking fitness isn't running fitness. They agree, mostly, and adjust your test for next year.

choices.label: Accept the number
choices.result: The number is the number. You accept it calmly and plan a better summer, and the strength coach nods, clearly surprised.

scenarios.title: The Pet
scenarios.text: You get a dog from the shelter, a big nervous mutt with one ear up, and it changes your schedule more than any coach ever has.

authoring.premise: You get a dog, and it changes your schedule more than you expected.

choices.label: Love the morning walks
choices.result: The morning walks become the calmest part of your day. The dog learns to wait at the door at six, and so, somehow, do you.

choices.label: Bring the dog on Fridays
choices.result: Fridays at the facility, with the dog. It becomes the team's dog within a month, and the linemen fight over who gets to walk it.

choices.label: Build it into the routine
choices.result: The dog, built into your routine like a stretching session, with walks before film. Everyone's happier, especially the dog, who now knows the playbook.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Account
scenarios.text: Your advisor finally gets you to open a retirement account, after three years of reminders. The paperwork is waiting on the table, with little yellow arrows.

authoring.premise: Your advisor finally gets you to open a retirement account.

choices.label: Do it right
choices.result: Done right: every arrow signed, every question asked, contributions set to grow on their own. Your advisor sends a photo of the paperwork, framed, as a joke.

choices.label: Ask {parent} what he wishes he'd done
choices.result: What does {parent} wish he'd done at your age? It's a long, honest talk on the phone, and it changes what you sign.

choices.label: Sign the minimum
choices.result: The minimum, signed and then forgotten about. Your advisor sighs on the phone and sets a reminder for the same day next year.

scenarios.title: The Charity Basketball Game
scenarios.text: A charity basketball game with teammates in a high school gym, and you are, by a wide margin, the worst player on the court. The crowd has noticed.

authoring.premise: A charity basketball game with teammates, and you're the worst player on the court.

choices.label: Play it for laughs
choices.result: Every miss, celebrated like a championship. The crowd loves it, the clips go around, and the charity raises more than it ever has.

choices.label: Practice for a week
choices.result: A week of secret practice in your driveway. You score twice in the game, and your teammates are genuinely amazed.

choices.label: Coach from the bench
choices.result: A clipboard, a whistle and the bench. You coach your team to a win, and the losing team demands a rematch.

scenarios.title: Supporting a Teammate's Cause
scenarios.text: A teammate is launching a foundation for kids in his old neighborhood and asks you to stand beside him. It's his cause, and he's nervous about it.

authoring.premise: A teammate asks you to support his foundation.

choices.label: Show up
choices.result: Every event this season, and you show up early to each one. He stops looking nervous by the third, and you help him with the speeches.

choices.label: Help with the plan
choices.result: You help him build the plan, not just the photos: a budget, a board, a calendar. A year later, it's still running.

choices.label: Donate quietly
choices.result: A quiet donation and your best wishes. He's grateful, and you can tell from his face that he hoped you'd stand beside him.

scenarios.title: The Old Rival on Your Team
scenarios.text: A kicker you competed with all through college signs with your club as a backup. He beat you for a scholarship once. Now he's the one on the practice squad.

authoring.premise: A kicker you competed with in college signs with your club as a backup.

choices.label: Bury the old rivalry
choices.result: Lunch on his first day, and the old rivalry turns into a joke you both share. By midseason, he's your best friend on the team.

choices.label: Stay ahead every day
choices.result: Ahead of him every day, by a little. He notices, you notice, and neither of you says a word about the scholarship.

choices.label: Help him fit in
choices.result: His introduction to the room, made by you, generously. The room notices how you handle it, and so does {coach}, who says nothing and remembers.

scenarios.title: The Brother's Wedding
scenarios.text: {sibling} is getting married on a game weekend. The date was set before the schedule came out, and {sibling} has already asked you to give the toast.

authoring.premise: {sibling} is getting married on a game weekend.

choices.label: Fly in for the wedding
choices.result: The Friday, granted by {coach}, a flight back Saturday night. You give the toast, and {sibling} doesn't stop crying through it.

choices.label: Help move the date
choices.result: A different date, found together with {sibling}, who moves it a week. You're there all weekend, and so is the rest of the family.

choices.label: Send a video toast
choices.result: A video toast, recorded in the locker room. {sibling} plays it twice, and you watch the reception on a phone in a hotel.

scenarios.title: The City Starts to Feel Like Home
scenarios.text: One morning you realize you know your neighbors' names, your barista knows your order, and the dry cleaner asks about your knee. The city has started to feel like home.

authoring.premise: You realize you know your neighbors and your coffee order.

choices.label: Put down roots
choices.result: A neighborhood group, a library card, a farmers' market on Saturdays. You start saying yes to things, and the city says yes back.

choices.label: Enjoy it quietly
choices.result: Quietly, you enjoy it. Home is a nice word, and you don't need to say it out loud to anyone to feel it.

choices.label: Think about staying for good
choices.result: A question you've never asked: what if you stayed here after football? You start reading about schools and neighborhoods at night.

scenarios.title: The Sponsor's Event
scenarios.text: Your sponsor wants you at a store opening on your only day off this month. It's three hours away, there's a ribbon to cut, and the regional manager has already announced you.

authoring.premise: Your sponsor wants you at an event on your only day off.

choices.label: Go and do it well
choices.result: You go, cut the ribbon, sign for two hours and smile until your face hurts. The sponsor is thrilled, and your day off disappears.

choices.label: Offer another day
choices.result: A different day, offered politely. They take it, and reschedule the ribbon, and the regional manager pretends it was his idea.

choices.label: Keep your day off
choices.result: No, politely, and you keep your day off. The sponsor is a little cooler next time, and you sleep until ten.

scenarios.title: The Mid-Career Check-In
scenarios.text: Your agent takes you to lunch and asks a question nobody's asked you before: where do you want to be in five years? Not the contract. The life.

authoring.premise: Your agent asks where you want to be in five years.

choices.label: Write it down
choices.result: The club, the house, the people, the life after, written on a napkin. Your agent keeps the napkin and brings it to every meeting.

choices.label: Aim for the top
choices.result: The top, you say: the best in the league, the biggest contract, the Hall of Fame. Your agent smiles and gets to work.

choices.label: Ask your family first
choices.result: Your family first, you say, and you ask them that night. Their answer surprises you, and it changes the next contract.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Gets Rich
scenarios.text: A teammate signs a huge contract and starts acting like it: the new watch, the entourage, the late arrivals, a new way of talking to the equipment staff.

authoring.premise: A teammate signs a huge contract and starts acting like it.

choices.label: Talk to him as a friend
choices.result: A quiet word, as a friend, in the parking lot. He hears it, eventually, and apologizes to the equipment staff on his own.

choices.label: Keep the room together
choices.result: The room, kept from turning on him. You defend him in public and push him in private, and by December he's himself again.

choices.label: Let him be
choices.result: Money changes people for a while, you decide, and you let him be. He comes back to earth by spring, mostly.

scenarios.title: The Practice Squad Kicker
scenarios.text: The practice squad kicker is good, really good, and the coaches know it. They've started watching his kicks as closely as yours, and he's started noticing.

authoring.premise: The practice squad kicker is good, and the coaches know it.

choices.label: Raise your level
choices.result: Your level, raised, and kept there. Every practice is better than the last, and the coaches start watching your kicks again.

choices.label: Help him anyway
choices.result: Help, freely given: his plant foot, his routine, his nerves. He'll get a job somewhere, and he'll remember who helped him.

choices.label: Ask where you stand
choices.result: {coach}, asked plainly where you stand. The answer is fair and a little uncomfortable, and you leave with a clear target.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Net in the Living Room
scenarios.text: You set up a kicking net in the living room for winter practice, right in front of the television. {love_interest} has opinions, mostly about the lamp that's already broken.

authoring.premise: You set up a net in the living room, and {love_interest} has opinions.

choices.label: Move it to the garage
choices.result: The net, moved to the garage, with a space heater. Peace returns to the house, the lamp is replaced, and the garage becomes your favorite room.

choices.label: Negotiate a deal
choices.result: A deal: weekdays only, and you hang the paintings that have been leaning on the wall since you moved in. Everyone wins.

choices.label: Keep the net
choices.result: The net stays where it is. Some arguments are worth having, you decide, and you kick very carefully around the brand-new lamp all winter.

scenarios.title: The Season-Ticket Holder
scenarios.text: A season-ticket holder has sat in the same seat behind the bench for thirty years, and talks to you every single week: weather, wind, his late wife's opinions on kickers.

authoring.premise: A season-ticket holder has sat behind the bench for thirty years and talks to you every week.

choices.label: Learn his story
choices.result: His story, over a dozen conversations: he was here for every era of this club, good and terrible. You start looking for him before warmups.

choices.label: Bring him onto the field
choices.result: A practice pass, arranged by you. He walks onto the field for the first time in thirty years and has to sit down.

choices.label: Wave every week
choices.result: A wave every week, and he waves back from his seat. It's small and steady, and you'd miss it terribly if it ever stopped.

scenarios.title: The Charity Visit You Remember
scenarios.text: A charity visit to the children's hospital leaves a mark. One kid, eight years old, asked you to kick a paper ball across his room, and you can't stop thinking about him.

authoring.premise: A charity visit leaves a mark, and you can't stop thinking about one kid.

choices.label: Go back on your own
choices.result: Back, on your own, without cameras, twice a month. The kid's family remembers you forever, and you remember them every time you see a paper ball.

choices.label: Start something
choices.result: A small fund for the hospital, started by you and run by a nurse. It buys games, tablets and paper balls, and it's still running years later.

choices.label: Keep his drawing in your locker
choices.result: His drawing of you, kicking a paper ball, goes in your locker. You look at it before every game, and it calms you more than any routine.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Staff Dinner
scenarios.text: The coaches invite you to dinner at the head coach's house, which they've never done before. You're the only player there, and there are place cards.

authoring.premise: The coaches invite you to dinner, which they've never done before.

choices.label: Go and enjoy it
choices.result: Dinner, stories and a long evening on the patio. They're people too, it turns out, and the head coach does a very bad impression of you.

choices.label: Go and listen closely
choices.result: Mostly listening, all evening. You learn what they think of the special teams, and what they think of you, and both are useful.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.result: A polite no. It feels strange to eat with the people who decide your job, and you're not sure that's a good reason.

scenarios.title: The Big Market Rumor
scenarios.text: A big-market club is rumored to want you next season. Your agent mentions it 'just so you know', and every reporter at your locker mentions it too.

authoring.premise: A big-market club is rumored to want you next season.

choices.label: Let the rumor be a rumor
choices.result: Silence, and no comment to anyone. The rumor stays a rumor, and you stay focused on this season, mostly, and the reporters move on.

choices.label: Reassure your club
choices.result: Your own club hears it from you directly: you're happy here. The general manager thanks you, and the front office remembers.

choices.label: Kick like it's an audition
choices.result: Fuel, every single week: you kick like the big-market club is watching every practice, because it probably is, and your leg has never felt better.

scenarios.title: The Weather Delay
scenarios.text: A lightning delay in the second quarter, and the teams go to the locker rooms for three hours. Your leg is cold by the first hour and stiff by the second.

authoring.premise: A long weather delay, and you have to stay warm for three hours.

choices.label: Plan the warmup with the trainers
choices.result: A warmup plan, built with the trainers: bike, bands, a heat pack every thirty minutes. You walk out loose and ready when the lights come back on.

choices.label: Keep the unit laughing
choices.result: Card tricks, bad jokes and an impression of {coach}. The specialists laugh through the whole delay, and three hours pass like one.

choices.label: Rest in the locker room
choices.result: A towel over your eyes, a bench, and rest. You nap for an hour, and you're fresh, if a little stiff, when they call you back.

scenarios.title: The Players' Council
scenarios.text: The players form a leadership council after a rough season, eight players, and they vote you on. The first meeting is Monday, and there's already a list of problems.

authoring.premise: The players form a leadership council, and you're on it.

choices.label: Commit to the council
choices.result: Every meeting, every follow-up, every hard conversation with management. The council fixes three real problems, and you lose a lot of sleep doing it.

choices.label: Bring data to every meeting
choices.result: Numbers, charts and dates to every single meeting. The coaches start listening to the council because of the data, and say so.

choices.label: Stay quiet on the council
choices.result: On the council, quietly, letting the others lead. You vote, you listen, and you're glad when the season ends and the meetings stop.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: The Middle Years
scenarios.text: A contract year in your thirties means proving you're not slowing down. The club has a younger kicker on the practice squad, and the general manager mentions it.

authoring.premise: At thirty, a contract year means proving you're not slowing down.

choices.label: Train like a rookie
choices.result: All summer, like a rookie: early, hard, hungry. You come back faster than you've been in three years, and the general manager notices.

choices.label: Show them the numbers
choices.result: Your numbers, shown to the club: as good as ever, better in the cold. They agree, grudgingly, and the conversation changes.

choices.label: Keep it calm at home
choices.result: Calm at home, on purpose: the contract will come or it won't. You sleep well, and your kicks feel easy.

scenarios.title: Doubts at Thirty
scenarios.text: A slump in your thirties, and the questions are all about your age, not your form. The analysts have started using the word 'decline', and a reporter asks about retirement.

authoring.premise: A slump at thirty, and the questions are about your age, not your form.

choices.label: Find the real cause in the film
choices.result: The real cause, found in the film after three nights: your plant foot, not your age. You fix it in a week and say nothing to the reporters.

choices.label: Kick two hundred a day
choices.result: Two hundred balls a day, every day, until the slump breaks. It does, on day eleven, and your leg feels every one of them.

choices.label: Lean on {holder}
choices.result: {holder}, who has seen you through everything, says simply that this is just another one. It helps more than any drill.

choices.label: Use the tools you learned
choices.result: The tools you learned the first time come right back: the breath, the word, the one thought. The slump is shorter, and the reporters move on.
choices.lock_text: having gotten help before

scenarios.title: The Thirty-Something Streak
scenarios.text: A month without a miss, and the stories say you're better than ever at thirty-two. The highlight shows have a graphic, and the specialists have stopped saying the word.

authoring.premise: A month without a miss, and the stories say you're better than ever.

choices.label: Stay in your routine
choices.result: Nothing changes: same breakfast, same warmup, same parking spot. You don't read a word of the stories, and the streak goes on.

choices.label: Share it with the unit
choices.result: The streak belongs to the snapper and {holder} too, and you say so in every interview. The specialists' chat is very happy.

choices.label: Enjoy it quietly at home
choices.result: A good dinner at home, the television off. You enjoy it the way you'd want to remember it, and {parent} calls to say he's proud.

scenarios.title: The Kicker They Drafted
scenarios.text: The club drafts a kicker in the middle rounds. He's watching your every kick from the sideline, taking notes, and he's very polite about it.

authoring.premise: The club drafts a kicker in the middle rounds, and he's watching your every kick.

choices.label: Give him a show
choices.result: Every practice, a quiet show: long, clean and calm. He takes a lot of notes, and so, you notice, do the coaches.

choices.label: Teach him
choices.result: Your routine, your wind charts, your nerves: you teach him all of it. The room notices, and so does {coach}.

choices.label: Ask {coach} the plan
choices.result: The plan, asked plainly in the hallway. {coach}'s answer is honest: you're the kicker, and he's the future. Both things are true.

scenarios.title: Hurt at Thirty
scenarios.text: An injury in your thirties, a groin strain on a routine kick, and the recovery takes longer than it used to. The trainers keep saying 'at your age', gently.

authoring.premise: An injury at thirty, and the recovery takes longer than it used to.

choices.label: Follow the plan exactly
choices.result: The plan, exactly, for six weeks. It takes longer than it would have at twenty-five, and you come back whole.

choices.label: Push to come back
choices.result: Back two weeks early, and sore. You kick carefully for a month, and the trainers watch every rep like hawks.

choices.label: Take extra time
choices.result: Extra time, on purpose. You come back fresh and a little behind, and your body thanks you for it all season.

choices.label: Use what you learned
choices.result: What you learned last time comes straight back: the order of the exercises, the warning signs, the patience. You're back on schedule and smarter.
choices.lock_text: having been through a hard recovery before

scenarios.title: The New Club at Thirty
scenarios.text: A new club, at thirty-one, and the young players already know your name. Some of them had your poster. One of them asks you to sign his old jersey.

authoring.premise: A new club, and the young players already know your name.

choices.label: Earn it anyway
choices.result: Earned anyway, one practice at a time, as if nobody knew you. The young players respect that more than the poster.

choices.label: Take the young specialists to lunch
choices.result: Lunch, the first week, with every young specialist. By Friday they're asking you everything, and you're the heart of the room.

choices.label: Focus on the job
choices.result: Just the job, quietly, and the rest follows on its own. You sign the old jersey, say very little else, and the young players respect it.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Patch
scenarios.text: You wear the captain's patch for the first time, sewn on by the equipment manager that morning. The whole team is watching to see what a kicker does with it.

authoring.premise: You wear the captain's patch for the first time.

choices.label: Lead by example

scenarios.title: The Holder Retires

scenarios.title: The Rookie's Holdout

authoring.premise: A rookie holds out, and the veterans want you to talk to him.

scenarios.title: The Charity Foundation Gala

authoring.premise: Your foundation holds its first gala.

scenarios.title: The Anniversary Trip

scenarios.title: The Marriage Counselor

scenarios.title: The Old College Friend's Wedding

authoring.premise: A college friend's wedding brings back the whole old crowd.

scenarios.title: The Old College Rival Retires

authoring.premise: A kicker you've competed with since college retires.

scenarios.title: A Kind Word From {tyler}

authoring.premise: {tyler} sends a message after a rough week, and it's kinder than you expected.

scenarios.title: The Player Rep Meeting

authoring.premise: The players' union holds a meeting about health care for retired players.

scenarios.title: The Players' Vote

scenarios.title: The Second Business

authoring.premise: You consider a second business, while the first is still finding its feet.

choices.label: Ask your first partner

scenarios.title: The Real Estate Pitch

scenarios.title: The Investment That Works

authoring.premise: An investment you made years ago starts paying off.

authoring.premise: You're audited, and every receipt from the last three years matters.
